limitations: Generalized cohort model used: this participant has no meal episodes in the training data, so no participant-specific calibration exists.
Research prototype; not medical advice and not for clinical decision-making.

The model learns glucose change at 30/60/90/120 minutes and the curve between those knots is linearly interpolated, so the reported peak time is resolved only to those knots and true peak timing may fall between them.
Prediction intervals are not calibrated, so no interval bounds are reported.
Drivers are reported at the 60-minute horizon, where this forecast peaks, and describe that horizon only.

This forecast averages an interpretable linear model (50%) with a gradient-boosted model (50%). The drivers below decompose the linear half exactly and are scaled by its weight; the boosted half has no exact additive decomposition and its contribution is NOT attributed here. Treat the listed drivers as a partial explanation.

These inputs were unavailable for this meal and were filled with training-set medians plus an explicit missing-value flag: g_dev_from_night, hr_mean_30min_bpm, minutes_since_prior_meal, prior_meal_carbs_g, q_retr_curve_spread, q_retr_delta_120, q_retr_delta_30, q_retr_delta_60, q_retr_delta_90, q_retr_mean_distance, q_retr_peak_delta, q_retr_ttp, r_hist_peak_delta, r_hist_per_carb, r_hist_recovery, r_hist_ttp.
Timestamps were expressed on this account's local clock, using its UTC offset at the meal time, so that time-of-day inputs match how the model was trained.
